title: Exertion (Kern ch. 12)
hookLine: the bodhisattvas vow to teach the sutra in hard times; Mahapajapati and Yasodhara are given promises

lines: A PROMISE WITH A WARNING LABEL.
cards: Here's a promise with a warning label. A crowd of bodhisattvas tells the Buddha: after you're gone, we'll keep teaching this sutra. Then, in the same breath, they describe how bad it will be.
People will be proud and hard to reach. They'll insult us, threaten us, throw some of us out. We'll keep going anyway.
It's a vow made with eyes open, after reading the forecast. And tucked into the same chapter, two women who have been watching get a promise of their own. You met them both in year one.

teach.h: WE'LL TEACH IT WHEN IT'S HARD.
teach.b: First, the vow. Two bodhisattvas, Bhaishajyaraja, the Medicine King, and Mahapratibhana, with their companions, promise to keep and teach this sutra after the Buddha's death, in an age when people will be hard to train.
Monks who've already received promises vow to teach it in other worlds.
Second, Mahaprajapati, called Mahapajapati in Pali: the Buddha's aunt, standing with a great company of nuns, gazing at him. He notices the look and asks, in paraphrase: why look at me so sadly?
Are you thinking I haven't named you? Then he names her. She too will become a Buddha, and the nuns with her.
Third, Yasodhara, the mother of Rahula. She thinks: he still hasn't mentioned my name. And he does: her own future buddhahood, spoken before everyone.
Both women are glad, and both vow to teach the sutra too. Fourth, the hard part. The Buddha looks at the bodhisattvas in silence, and they understand what he's asking.

teach.h: INSULTS, STICKS, AND NO TURNING BACK.
teach.b: In the fearful time to come, people will abuse us, threaten us with sticks and swords, and call us heretics. Some of the proud ones wearing robes will mock us and drive us out.

We'll bear it. We don't cling to body or life; we care for the path. That's exertion here: not a burst of energy on a good morning, but the decision to keep going when the conditions are named and they're bad.
And in the middle of it, the women watching from the side are seen, and named.

how: In Mahayana communities that keep the Lotus Sutra, the bodhisattvas' vow in this chapter is recited as a model of patient effort, and Mahaprajapati and Yasodhara are remembered as receiving their own promise of buddhahood.

o: the vow to keep going when hard times are named ahead
a burst of energy on a good, easy morning
a contest to see who can meditate the longest

games.q: in hard times: tap the pairs.
p: vows to teach after the Buddha's death
the Buddha's aunt, gazing at him
what the bodhisattvas say they'll bear

s: the bodhisattvas promise to teach only when times are good
they name the hard times ahead, insults and threats included, and vow to keep going.
the Buddha notices Mahaprajapati's look and speaks to her
he asks why she looks at him so, and then names her future buddhahood.
Yasodhara is left out of the promises
she thinks he hasn't named her, and then he does.

games.q: you're Mahaprajapati. promise after promise has gone out, and none to you. you're standing with the nuns, looking at the Buddha. what happens next?
o: you keep looking, and he speaks to you first.
you call out and demand to be named.
games.why: she says nothing. the Buddha notices her look, asks if she thinks she's been left out, and names her future buddhahood, and the nuns' with her.

practice: Feel your feet or your seat, and bring to mind one hard thing in your life right now. Don't solve it; just name it plainly, the way the bodhisattvas named the bad times ahead.
Then find one small piece of it you can keep doing, one call, one page, one meal cooked, and hold that, breath by breath.

wordCard.voice: Exertion. In chapter twelve, the vow to keep teaching when the times are named and they're hard, and two women seen and given their promise. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: energy, effort, steady exertion; one of the perfections a bodhisattva practices.

carryVoice: Your line: in hard times. The forecast was bad, and they promised anyway. See you tomorrow.
